chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah sanctified His Haram (sanctuary), that its emptiness should not be trodden upon, or its trees should not be cut down, except for Al-Idhkhir, or its birds should not be hunted.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific prohibitions regarding the sanctity of Makkah's Haram according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific sanctities (haram) of the Kaaba as declared by Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), prohibiting treading on its empty spaces, cutting its trees, and hunting its birds, with a specific exception for the plant Idhkhir. It highlights the divine preservation of Makkah's natural ecosystem as a sign of Allah's majesty, reinforcing the spiritual and physical inviolability of the sanctuary in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ib Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sanctified His<sup>azwj</sup> Al-Harram, from it being vacated and being empty, or its trees to be tampered with except for Al-Izkhir (a fragrant tropical grass), or its birds from being hunted’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following:
“I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Allah has made His House sacred. He has prohibited uprooting of its grass, cutting down of its trees, except al-Idhkhir, and hunting its birds.’”
